'''Center Parc Stadium''' (also commonly referred to as '''Georgia State Stadium''' or '''GSU Stadium''', formerly Turner Field) is an outdoor [[stadium]] in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]]. The stadium is the home of the [[Georgia State Panthers football|Georgia State Panthers football team]] as of the [[2017 Georgia State Panthers football team|2017 season]], replacing the [[Georgia Dome]] which had served as their home stadium from the [[2010 Georgia State Panthers football team|program's inception in 2010]] until [[2016 Georgia State Panthers football team|2016]].<ext><name>ref</name><attr/><inner>{{cite news|url=https://www.myajc.com/sports/college/how-turner-field-turned-into-georgia-state-football-stadium/51rCHI3icSYBTzZVNBQe9I/|title=How Turner Field turned into Georgia State's football stadium|author=Tim Tucker|newspaper=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|access-date=28 February 2019}}</inner><close></ref></close></ext>

It was originally built for the [[1996 Summer Olympics]] as [[Centennial Olympic Stadium]]. Following the [[1996 Summer Paralympics]], the Olympic Stadium was reconfigured as designed into the baseball-specific [[Turner Field]], serving as the home of the [[Atlanta Braves]] of [[Major League Baseball]] from [[1997 Atlanta Braves season|1997]] until [[2016 Atlanta Braves season|2016]]. After the Braves' departure for [[Truist Park]] in [[Cobb County, Georgia|Cobb County]], Georgia State University acquired the stadium and its surrounding parking lots for a large scale expansion of the university's campus, including new private and student housing, academic, and retail space, in addition to the stadium redevelopment.

Center Parc Stadium is the second former Braves ballpark to be converted to a college football stadium, the first being [[Boston University Terriers football|Boston University]]'s [[Nickerson Field]].<ext><name>ref</name><attr/><inner>{{Cite web|url=https://ballparkdigest.com/2016/09/08/turner-field-follows-in-footsteps-of-braves-field/|title = Turner Field Follows in Footsteps of Braves Field &#124; Ballpark Digest|date = 8 September 2016}}</inner><close></ref></close></ext></root>

'''U.S. Bank Stadium''' is an [[indoor stadium]] in [[Minneapolis]], Minnesota, U.S. Opened in 2016, the stadium was built on the former site of the [[Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome]] and is the home venue of the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). It also hosts early season [[college baseball]] games of the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers baseball|Minnesota Golden Gophers]].

The Vikings played at the Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome from [[1982 Minnesota Vikings season|1982]] until its closure in 2013; during construction, the Vikings played two seasons ([[2014 Minnesota Vikings season|2014]], [[2015 Minnesota Vikings season|2015]]) at the open-air [[Huntington Bank Stadium]] on the campus of the [[University of Minnesota]].<ext><name>ref</name><attr/><inner>{{cite web |title=Metrodome Next|url=http://www.msfc.com/tour.cfm|publisher=[[Metropolitan Sports Facilities Commission]]|access-date=March 15, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100210094221/http://www.msfc.com/tour.cfm|archive-date=February 10, 2010|url-status=dead}}</inner><close></ref></close></ext>

It was the first [[indoor stadium]] built in the NFL since [[Ford Field]] in Detroit, which opened in [[2002 NFL season|2002]]. As of March 2015, the overall budget was estimated to be $1.061&nbsp;billion, with $348&nbsp;million from the state of Minnesota, $150&nbsp;million from the city of Minneapolis, and $551&nbsp;million from the team and private contributions.<ext><name>ref</name><attr> name="Cost"</attr></ext> U.S. Bank Stadium hosted [[Super Bowl LII]] won by the [[2017 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] on February 4, 2018,<ext><name>ref</name><attr> name="superbowllii"</attr><inner>{{cite news|last=Patra|first=Kevin|title=Super Bowl LII Headed to Minnesota|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/super-bowl-lii-headed-to-minnesota-0ap2000000352335|publisher=[[National Football League]]|date=May 20, 2014|access-date=May 20, 2014}}</inner><close></ref></close></ext> the [[ESPN]] [[X Games]] on July 19–22, 2018, and the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA Final Four]] won by [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]]. In 2023, ''[[The Athletic]]'' ranked U.S. Bank Stadium as the top NFL venue.<ext><name>ref</name><attr/><inner>{{cite news |last1=Machota |first1=Jon |title=NFL stadium rankings: All 30 NFL venues from best to worst |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4783340/2023/08/21/nfl-stadium-rankings-all-30-nfl-venues-from-best-to-worst/ |website=The Athletic |access-date=August 22, 2023}}</inner><close></ref></close></ext></root>
